subject: Request: temporary autopin/grace-period for canary rollout to meet SLA
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@avasolutions.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production risk during next canary — need autopin/grace period for SLA

Laura,

Quick note from our ops team — we have a migration scheduled next week that will trigger a canary deployment for the transformer-based reranker. Our internal SLO is 99.9% p95 < 800ms and the customer explicitly requires a hold-harmless window for 72 hours after rollout to avoid cascading retries.

We saw a ~1.8% P50->P95 skew in last month's deployment and cannot tolerate repeated tail latency regressions during this migration. Can Redwood temporarily enable an autopin/grace-period policy so that if the canary shows any sustained p95 deterioration beyond our thresholds it will immediately fall back to the pinned stable version (or pin the old version until verified)? We need this change to be operational by Monday to align with our cutover.

Please advise what telemetry thresholds you can guarantee, what the fallback latency is, and whether this needs a formal SLA amendment or exception. I can loop in procurement if needed.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Ops, Ava Solutions
attachments: prod-telemetry-snippets.txt
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@avasolutions.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-14T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production risk during next canary — need autopin/grace period for SLA

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the telemetry snippet. We can move quickly but need to align infra, product, and legal. High level proposal below; I want internal sign-off by EOD today so we can confirm a path forward.

Proposal (short):
- Temporary autopin flag for the canary deployment that allows automatic fallback to the prior stable model when one or more guardrail conditions are met (see thresholds below). The flag is time-limited (72 hours) and reversible.
- Guardrail triggers (initial suggestion): sustained p95 latency > 1,000 ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows OR error rate (5xx) > 1.5% sustained for 2 minutes.
- When triggered: immediate traffic re-route to the pinned version + automated alert to both teams; telemetry TTL for decision should be <= 30s (we'll try to get it to 15s).
- Fallback will not auto-escalate deployment rollbacks to other regions without manual approval.

Markus — can you confirm feasibility and expected time to enable the autopin flag on the next canary?
Grace — from the account perspective, do we need a temporary SLA amendment or a credits-based carve-out for the 72-hour window?

If this is acceptable to Ava, we'll prepare a short amendment and a runbook for the ops team.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success (Redwood Inference)
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-14T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production risk during next canary — need autopin/grace period for SLA

Laura / team — technical notes below. Short answer: yes, we can ship an autopin capability quickly, but there are a few constraints and trade-offs to call out.

What we can do (implementation):
- Add a rollout-policy flag (autopin=true) scoped to the canary job. When triggered it will: 1) immediately divert 100% of traffic for the affected route to the previous pinned model instance pool, 2) set an automatic pin on the prior version for a configured grace_period (default 72h).
- Telemetry: we can expose p95, p99, and error-rate signals at 15s resolution if the canary is deployed into a telemetry-enabled pool. For non-telemetry pools there is a ~45s lag. The flag will only accept deployments into pools with full telemetry attached.

Caveats and risk:
- Cold-cache impact: immediate reroute will cause KV cache misses on the fallback model; we expect a transient tail increase for ~2-3 minutes. Recommend warming the pinned model prior to activation.
- Stateful changes: if a canary introduces incompatible tokenizer/embedding changes there may be request failures that are not mitigated by autopin — we must verify model compatibility.
- Race conditions: if multiple regions trigger simultaneously we need a global coordination lock; otherwise we risk flip-flopping. We'll implement a coordination mutex but it adds ~10s to the divert path.

Operational plan & ETA:
- Code + rollout-policy config: 1 business day (we can push a hotfix tomorrow morning).
- QA + small internal canary: half day.
- Documentation + runbook: same day as code.

Connor — can you prepare a short runbook that includes cache-warm steps and the telemetry dashboard URLs? I'll attach recommended thresholds in the spreadsheet.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
attachments: canary_thresholds.xlsx
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-14T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production risk during next canary — need autopin/grace period for SLA

Team — from account side, a pragmatic path helps Ava move forward and keeps contract risk low. Two items:

1) SLA amendment vs credits: I recommend we avoid a formal SLA rewrite if possible. Offer: temporary autopin policy + a capped SLA credit (0.5% of monthly invoice) if we cannot restore p95 within the 72-hour window and the root cause is on our side. That gets Ava the operational protection they want without a full legal amendment.

2) Documentation + acceptance: we'll send a 1-page operational addendum that describes triggers, fallback behavior, and expected cold-cache impact. If Ava accepts, we can implement autopin immediately after the DocuSign signature. I can draft the addendum and attach a redline so procurement has something concrete.

Samir — I attached a redline of the short addendum and the telemetry snippets you sent. Please let me know if procurement needs a different contact or if legal should be looped in.

Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales

Samir — following up with the confirmed internal plan. We have approval to enable the autopin rollout-policy for your upcoming canary subject to these final items:

- Ava confirmation of the telemetry pool (must be telemetry-enabled).
- DocuSign on the 1-page addendum (Grace to send).
- A short pre-cutover window (30 minutes) to warm caches for the pinned model; Connor will provide warm-up commands and dashboard links.

Links: INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1289
Runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Kp-autopin-draft

If you accept these items, we'll enable the flag tomorrow morning and run a short internal sanity canary. Please reply with an explicit OK by EOD tomorrow so we can meet your Monday migration.
